note:
The storefront ladder. Sales & Platforms owns getting the game onto a surface a player can reach it on, and owns what each one demands before it will take us. Every requirement here is either derived from the repo or explicitly marked as a judgment nobody has made yet — the point of the ladder is to say what the NEXT storefront costs before anyone commits to it, not to imply we are pursuing all of them.

Status is derived; 'pursuing' is the CEO's call and is deliberately null where he has not made it.

'blocks_publish' marks a requirement without which the build cannot reach a player at all, as against one we simply want. Analytics is not a publishing requirement — conflating the two made a live, perfectly publishable storefront read as broken.

platforms.name: itch.io — browser
platforms.note: The one place a player can reach the game today.

check.says_false: there is no Web export preset

requirements.label: A publish pipeline that runs on a tag

check.says_true: butler pushes the build on a tag
the workflow reads a publishing key from repository secrets

requirements.label: Store analytics we can read
requirements.note: The API key exists as a product; we have not asked for one. This is the only demand signal available to this studio today.

platforms.name: Android — Play Store
platforms.note: The tablet already runs a debug build. A public one is a different animal.

check.says_false: there is no Android export preset

requirements.label: A release signing key

check.says_false: only the debug keystore exists — a public build cannot be signed

requirements.note: Lose this key after publishing and the app can never be updated again; the store will not accept a differently-signed version. Where it lives is a personal-custody decision.

check.reason: Nothing in this repo can see whether a developer account exists.
check.would_need: Your word, recorded once — it costs a one-off fee and an identity check.

requirements.label: An age rating and a privacy policy

check.reason: Both are questionnaires on the store's own site, not artifacts here.
check.would_need: The store's rating questionnaire completed, and a privacy policy hosted somewhere public.

platforms.name: Steam
platforms.note: Where a paid PC release would live, and the only storefront with a wishlist worth forecasting from.

check.says_false: there is no desktop export preset at all

requirements.label: A Steamworks account and app fee

check.would_need: A decision to spend the one-off app fee, which is recoupable but real money.

requirements.label: A store page — capsules, trailer, copy

check.reason: None of it exists; the only public copy in this repo is the itch page.
check.would_need: Capsule art at several sizes, a trailer, and store copy — the largest art and video ask this project has ever had.

requirements.label: A wishlist number to forecast from

check.reason: There is no store page, so there is no wishlist. This is the number a launch forecast is built on, and it does not exist yet.
check.would_need: A published store page, and then Marketing driving traffic to it.

platforms.name: iOS
platforms.note: Furthest away, and the only one blocked by hardware.

check.says_false: there is no iOS export preset

requirements.label: A Mac to build and sign on

check.reason: Godot emits an Xcode project rather than an artifact, and none of it can be done from Linux.
check.would_need: A Mac. The runbook says so plainly; testing on your own device needs only Xcode and a cable, but shipping needs the whole chain.
